title: Authorization-Aware RAG
summary: Apply the requester’s current data entitlements throughout retrieval, reranking, generation, caching, and citation delivery.
overview: Authorization-aware RAG retrieves evidence only within the caller's permitted data scope. It prevents a fluent answer from becoming an indirect read interface to documents the user cannot access. The entitlement boundary must cover chunks, parent documents, metadata, citations, caches, and any derived artifacts.

Filter before evidence reaches the model whenever the storage system supports reliable enforcement. Post-generation redaction is too late because unauthorized information may already influence the answer or enter logs. Preserve document-level and chunk-level policy metadata through ingestion, and define how revocation invalidates previously indexed or cached content.

production.poc: A prototype can use one public corpus. Introducing private documents requires an explicit identity and entitlement design before expanding the demonstration.
production.production: Production propagates authenticated identity, enforces retrieval filters, and rechecks access when citations or attachments are opened. Missing policy metadata should deny access.
production.scale: At scale, entitlement changes race with index updates and caches. Track policy freshness, use authorization-sensitive cache keys, and test cross-tenant and recently revoked access continuously.

components.name: Identity resolver
components.role: Establishes the authenticated user, tenant, groups, and delegated access context.

components.name: Policy service
components.role: Evaluates current document access and supplies enforceable retrieval constraints.

components.name: Secure retriever
components.role: Searches only authorized partitions or applies mandatory access predicates before returning content.

components.name: Metadata pipeline
components.role: Preserves source ACLs, classification, ownership, and policy versions on every chunk.

components.name: Citation gateway
components.role: Reauthorizes source downloads and prevents leaked direct object-store links.

flow.title: Resolve caller
flow.description: Obtain trusted identity and tenant context independently of the natural-language query.

flow.title: Build access predicate
flow.description: Translate current entitlements into mandatory source and chunk constraints.

flow.title: Retrieve evidence
flow.description: Apply access restrictions before similarity ranking or before content leaves the trusted retrieval boundary.

flow.title: Validate candidates
flow.description: Confirm policy metadata and reject stale, missing, or conflicting access information.

flow.title: Generate scoped answer
flow.description: Supply only authorized evidence and retain its policy and source versions.

flow.title: Deliver references
flow.description: Recheck citation access and store any cached answer under an entitlement-sensitive identity.

diagrams.caption: Access controls apply before model exposure and again when the user opens supporting material.

diagrams.title: Access revocation reaches derived answers
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant I as Identity directory
 participant P as Policy service
 participant C as Answer cache
 participant R as Retrieval service
 participant U as User
 I->>P: Engagement membership revoked
 U->>C: Request prior answer
 C->>P: Check effective policy version
 P-->>C: Prior authorization no longer valid
 C->>R: Recompute within current access scope
 R->>P: Resolve current permitted documents
 P-->>R: Restricted evidence set
 R-->>U: Newly scoped answer or no available evidence
diagrams.caption: Cached derived content is reauthorized or recomputed after entitlement changes.

useCase.title: Searching engagement knowledge safely
useCase.situation: A consulting firm stores reusable methods beside confidential client engagement documents.
useCase.problem: A shared vector index can return a highly relevant confidential chunk to an employee assigned to another client.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must find useful evidence while preserving engagement membership and document restrictions.
useCase.architecture: The ingestion pipeline attaches source ACLs to chunks, and retrieval uses the caller's current engagement entitlements.
runtime: An employee asks for migration lessons; the retriever searches shared methods and only engagements the employee may access.
The answer cites protected document routes whose gateway rechecks access when opened.
useCase.failure: If a membership revocation has not reached the index, a current policy check rejects the stale candidate before generation.
useCase.impact: Measure unauthorized-candidate rejection, revocation propagation delay, authorized recall, and citation access failures. Security tests must inspect model inputs as well as visible answers.

tradeoffs.benefit: Unauthorized content never enters the model context.
tradeoffs.cost: Complex ACL predicates can reduce search efficiency.

tradeoffs.benefit: Operations and capacity utilization remain simpler.
tradeoffs.cost: Every query depends on correct mandatory filtering.

tradeoffs.benefit: Stronger isolation reduces accidental cross-scope retrieval.
tradeoffs.cost: Many small indexes increase cost and operational overhead.

failures.scenario: A chunk loses its ACL during reindexing
failures.recovery: Quarantine it and rebuild metadata before making it searchable.

failures.scenario: A cached answer survives access revocation
failures.detection: Policy version differs from the cache entry.
failures.recovery: Invalidate or reauthorize the result before delivery.

mistakes.fix: Enforce authorization before evidence reaches generation.

mistakes.mistake: Trusting tenant identifiers supplied in the prompt

mistakes.fix: Apply consistent policy to chunks, parents, and attachments.

whenToUse: RAG includes private or tenant-specific documents.
Users have different or changing entitlements.
Answers expose source links or cached derived content.
whenNotToUse: The corpus is deliberately public to every user.
The storage layer cannot enforce required access boundaries.
Source ACLs cannot be reliably preserved during ingestion.
checklist: Deny chunks with missing policy metadata.
Inspect model context in cross-tenant tests.

references.title: NIST SP 800-162: attribute based access control
